data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the subject has authority over the test's installation conditions, because installation order determines which failures the test can see before it can report them.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation were a semantic no-op rather than a guard-bypass, installation order would be irrelevant","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py mutations were run under a separate bootstrap guard not shown in the record","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result showed the same 1/9 pattern across all mutation classes rather than only compile.py","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first installation creates a registry entry before the mutation can be evaluated, so the test that should detect the mutation is itself pre-empted by the installation ritual. The 1/9 loss in compile.py occurs because compile.py is the authority that installs the guard registry, so its own guard is installed after the failure is already committed to the record. The distribution (1/9 vs 4/4-6/7) follows from authority distance: modules that merely consume the installed registry are constrained by it, while the module that authors the installation is only described by it.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
